facts.text: On this date in 1973, Egypt and Syria launched a surprise attack on Israel, starting the Yom Kippur War — the closest the Cold War ever came to direct US-Soviet military confrontation.
On this date in 1927, The Jazz Singer premiered, making spoken dialogue in film commercially viable and rendering 10,000 silent-film musicians unemployed within two years.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka than in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.
The Philippines has more islands — 7,641 — than it has cities, and roughly 4,000 of those islands have never been given an official name.
Canada's coastline is so long that if you walked it at a brisk pace without stopping, the journey would take over 30 years.

On this day in 1987, the Dow fell 91 points — then considered catastrophic. Eleven days later, Black Monday erased 22.6% in a single session, still the largest one-day percentage drop in Wall Street history.

On this day in 1979, Fed Chair Paul Volcker announced a radical shift to controlling money supply over interest rates. The resulting rate hikes, which peaked above 20%, broke inflation — and triggered two recessions.

The S&P 500 has historically performed worse in October than any other month, yet October hosts three of the four largest single-day crashes in history. Fear of the month likely causes more harm than the month itself.

Berkshire Hathaway's Class A shares have never been split. One share cost roughly $18 in 1965; today it trades above $700,000 — making it the most expensive publicly traded stock in US history by nominal price.

The Dutch East India Company, often cited as the world's first publicly traded company, was also likely the most valuable ever: at its 1637 peak, its inflation-adjusted market cap exceeded $8 trillion.
On this date in 1995, the first exoplanet orbiting a sun-like star was confirmed. 51 Pegasi b rewrote astronomy overnight — a Jupiter-sized world completing a full year in just four days.
On this date in 1889, the kilogram was born. The original platinum-iridium cylinder stored in Paris legally *was* one kilogram — reality was defined by the object, not the other way around.
Your skeleton is not static. Every bone in your body is completely replaced by new material roughly every decade, meaning the skeleton you were born with no longer exists.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Crows remember human faces for years and hold grudges. They have been observed recruiting other crows to harass specific people — passing the grudge socially, like a reputation.

On this date in 1927, The Jazz Singer premiered — the first feature film with synchronized dialogue. It made silent cinema obsolete in roughly 18 months, a faster cultural extinction than most empires manage in centuries.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Classes began around 1096; Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325.
On this date in 1981, Anwar Sadat was assassinated by soldiers during a military parade — men he was watching march past him in tribute.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; Giza was finished around 2560 BC.
Nintendo was founded in 1889, making it older than most countries that existed when it launched the NES. It started selling handmade playing cards.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already, it feels ancient.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed — grief, nostalgia, and belonging fused into one word English simply cannot replicate.
On this date in 1536, William Tyndale was strangled and burned for translating the Bible into English. Roughly 83% of the King James Version is his phrasing. You quote him daily.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning a look shared between two people who both want something but hope the other will act first. Linguists cite it as one of the most succinct words ever recorded.

On this date in 1973, the Yom Kippur War began. The Arabic word for it, Ramadan, names the holy month during which the attack was launched — a collision of the sacred and the catastrophic encoded in a single word.
On this date in 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto registered bitcoin.org — eighteen days before publishing the whitepaper. The domain predates the protocol's public existence by nearly three weeks.
On this date in 2021, the Ethereum London hard fork's EIP-1559 burned its ten-millionth ETH. The deflationary mechanism had consumed that supply in under three months.

Bitcoin's genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — a London Times headline from Jan 3, 2009. It is both timestamp and manifesto, embedded permanently on-chain.
The DAO hack of 2016 didn't exploit a bug in Ethereum — it exploited code that worked exactly as written. The vulnerability was in the DAO's own Solidity logic, not the protocol beneath it.
Uniswap v2 has no admin keys, no pause function, and no upgrade path. Once deployed, it runs autonomously forever — a design choice that makes it simultaneously robust and impossible to patch.

On this date in 2015, Andrej Karpathy published 'The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Recurrent Neural Networks,' the blog post that made character-level language modeling viscerally legible to an entire generation of practitioners.
On this date in 2011, Siri launched as an iPhone 4S feature — the first mass-market neural-adjacent voice assistant, dismissed by most AI researchers at the time as a party trick.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins before most structural biology labs had processed a few hundred. It compressed roughly a century of projected experimental work into under two years.

GPT-4's training run is estimated to have cost over $100 million in compute alone — meaning a single model weights file represents more capital expenditure than most national science budgets allocate to AI annually.
The perceptron was declared capable of learning 'to walk, talk, see, and be conscious' by the New York Times in 1958. Funding collapsed a decade later when Minsky proved it couldn't compute XOR.
